Plasma spraying can apply the metallic bond coating layer in either an air environment or a protective atmosphere, depending on the component temperature requirements.
Low-pressure plasma spraying (LPPS) of the bond coating layer results in better bond strength and oxidation resistance compared to conventional air plasma spraying.
Plasma-sprayed ceramic layers are typically applied at metal temperatures of 100-300°C to avoid compressive thermal expansion mismatch stresses.
Plasma-sprayed zirconia coatings develop a columnar solidification microstructure that requires thermal cycling to fully develop the desired subcritical microcracking.
As-sprayed 8% yttria-stabilized zirconia has a tensile/compressive modulus of 7-35 GPa, well below the 154 GPa value for 95% dense polycrystalline stabilized zirconia.
EB-PVD TBCs require smooth, preferably polished, surfaces for optimal adhesion through chemical bonding at higher deposition temperatures of 870-1090°C.
EB-PVD zirconia coatings have a columnar microstructure with intercolumnar structural discontinuities to accommodate strains.
Laser-glazed EB-PVD zirconia coatings have exhibited low rates of erosion compared to plasma-sprayed and unglazed EB-PVD zirconia.
Fracture toughness values for plasma-sprayed and EB-PVD TBC systems are typically in the range of 0.5 to 3.2 MPa√m.
Zirconia spalling can be caused by both tensile and compressive strains in the TBC system.
This 60-month NASA-funded program aims to develop thermomechanical and thermochemical life prediction models for plasma-sprayed and EB-PVD TBC systems.
The program will obtain statistically significant design data and validate the life prediction models through engine testing.
The program focuses on TBC systems produced by commercial suppliers Chromalloy, Klock, and Temescal.
The first year of the program involved a literature review, specimen procurement, and initial characterization and testing of the TBC systems.
Eddy current technology has been shown to be feasible for nondestructively measuring the zirconia layer thickness in TBC systems.
